title: Applewood Turkey Cutlets with Maple-Sage Gravy
description: Thin turkey breast cutlets poach in applewood-smoked broth and receive an extra ladle of maple-sage gravy.
equipment: Small enamel Dutch oven with tight lid, sized to hold the food snugly

ingredients.name: unenhanced skinless turkey breast cutlets
ingredients.note: Thin cutlets with no injected brine.

ingredients.name: low-sodium turkey broth
ingredients.note: Use plain broth made from meat, bones and water, with no added vegetable blend or seasonings.

ingredients.name: smooth Löwensenf Bavarian mustard
ingredients.note: Pass through a fine sieve if visibly grainy.

ingredients.name: hot drinking water
ingredients.note: Keep ready; use only as needed to maintain liquid depth or make up the sauce measure.

steps.title: Heat the Traeger
steps.text: Preheat the Traeger Silverton 610 to 275°F with apple pellets, about 15 minutes with the lid closed.

steps.title: Warm the braising liquid
steps.text: Bring {broth} with {sage} just to a simmer in the open Dutch oven on the stove, about 3–6 minutes.

steps.title: Smoke the braising liquid
steps.text: Move the uncovered pot to the Traeger grate. Close the smoker lid and smoke the liquid for 15 minutes.

steps.title: Even the cutlets
steps.text: Place {turkey} between sheets of parchment and gently flatten the thick ends with a small skillet to a uniform 1/3 inch.

steps.title: Cover with broth
steps.text: Lay the cutlets in the smoked broth without overlapping. Add {topup} if needed to just cover. Fit the lid now. These thin cutlets need no stall wrap.

steps.title: Poach to temperature
steps.text: Poach covered at 275°F for 8–20 minutes, checking from 8 minutes. Insert the probe sideways into each center and remove each cutlet to a covered dish with warm juices as it reaches 165°F.

steps.title: Rest in the juices
steps.text: Rest the covered cutlets off heat for 3 minutes.

steps.title: Reserve extra gravy
steps.text: Discard the sage and measure 1 cup of the poaching liquid into the HexClad, adding {topup} if needed.

steps.title: Season the gravy
steps.text: Stir {maple} and {mustard} into the poaching liquid.

steps.title: Thicken the sauce
steps.text: Bring the skillet liquid to a boil. Whisk in the stirred slurry and simmer for 1 minute, stirring, until the sauce coats the back of a spoon.

steps.title: Enrich the gravy
steps.text: Swirl {butter} into the skillet off heat.

steps.title: Serve generously
steps.text: Slice the tenderized cutlets thinly across the grain. Spoon half the gravy onto the plates, lay the slices in it and spoon the rest over their tops.

notes: Make ahead: Flatten and refrigerate the cutlets up to a day ahead, then poach close to serving. For dairy-free gravy omit the butter. For a gentler flavor omit the mustard. Refrigerate promptly in shallow portions and use within 3 days. Freezer-Friendly Verdict: Yes. Freeze individual portions surrounded by sauce for up to 2 months to protect their moisture. Fridge reheat: Place one portion with its sauce in a covered shallow dish. Install the bottom drip pan in the APO and preheat to 325°F, sous vide mode off, rear heat on, top and bottom off, 60% steam. Set the probe to 165°F in the center. Start checking after 12 minutes and heat until 165°F throughout. Freezer reheat: Thaw overnight in the refrigerator. Follow the fridge reheating directions and stir the sauce smooth.
